subject: Biology

stem: A wound-healing treatment was applied to cultured skin. Lesion area and the percentage of fibroblasts expressing gene R were measured.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Describe the change in lesion area.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Outline how image analysis could measure lesion percentage.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Evaluate reliability if each mean is based on five cultures.

parts.label: d
parts.html: Calculate the percentage-point fall in gene-R-positive cells in treated tissue.

parts.label: e
parts.html: Suggest why a housekeeping gene is also measured.

parts.label: f
parts.html: Deduce a possible relationship between gene R and repair.

questions.title: Skin repair and gene expression

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: Lesion area decreases in both groups; treated tissue decreases faster and reaches 18% compared with 47% in the control.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: Measure lesion pixels/area and total sampled area using a scale; calculate lesion area divided by total area x100 using consistent thresholds.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: Replication allows a mean but n=5 is small; no error bars/raw variation are given, so repeat with more independent cultures.

solparts.label: d
solparts.html: 64 - 29 = 35 percentage points.

solparts.label: e
solparts.html: Provides a stable reference/control for sample amount and overall transcription.

solparts.label: f
solparts.html: Gene-R expression falls as repair progresses; it may promote early fibroblast activity/inflammation, but correlation alone does not establish causation.

stem: The genome of a marine worm contains 18% cytosine.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Calculate the expected percentage of thymine in double-stranded DNA.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Name the method used to amplify a specific DNA region.

parts.label: c
parts.html: State two differences between DNA and RNA.

questions.title: DNA and RNA

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: Polymerase chain reaction / PCR.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: DNA has deoxyribose and thymine and is usually double-stranded; RNA has ribose and uracil and is usually single-stranded. Any two.

stem: A plasma membrane separates cytoplasm from extracellular fluid.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Explain why the membrane is described as a mosaic.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Describe phospholipid arrangement.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Explain simple diffusion of oxygen across the membrane.

questions.title: Fluid mosaic membranes

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: Different proteins/glycoproteins/glycolipids are distributed through the phospholipid bilayer.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: Hydrophilic phosphate heads face aqueous solutions; hydrophobic fatty-acid tails face inward; molecules form a bilayer and can move laterally.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: Oxygen is small/non-polar and dissolves in the hydrophobic core; it moves down its concentration gradient without ATP.

stem: Pressure changes produced by respiratory muscles move air into and out of the lungs.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Explain how diaphragm contraction causes inhalation.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Name the intercostal muscles that contract during quiet inhalation.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Explain two roles of alveolar surfactant.

questions.title: Ventilation

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: Diaphragm flattens, thoracic volume increases, pressure falls below atmospheric pressure and air enters.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: External intercostal muscles.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: Reduces surface tension and prevents alveolar collapse; helps keep alveoli open and reduces work of breathing.

stem: A grassland food web contains grasses, insects, small birds, hawks, fungi and bacteria.
Answer 1 of the following questions. One additional construction mark is available for each response.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Define autotroph.

parts.label: b
parts.html: State the ecological role of fungi and bacteria.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Explain why energy transfer between trophic levels is inefficient.

parts.label: d
parts.html: Explain how livestock farming may contribute to climate change.

questions.title: Energy flow and ecosystems

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: An organism that uses light or chemical energy to synthesize organic compounds from inorganic substances.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: They are decomposers/saprotrophs that digest dead organic matter and recycle mineral nutrients.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: Energy is lost as heat in respiration and in waste/uneaten material; only a small fraction becomes new biomass.

solparts.label: d
solparts.html: Ruminants release methane; manure/fertilizer can release greenhouse gases; land clearing reduces carbon storage, strengthening the greenhouse effect.

stem: Crop production depends on insect pollinators, but populations are declining in some regions.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Explain why glucose is transported readily in plants and animals.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Discuss human actions that threaten and conserve pollinators.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Explain evolution of pesticide resistance.

questions.title: Pollinators, food security and evolution

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: Glucose is polar/soluble in water; transported in blood or phloem sap; provides an immediate respiratory substrate; can be converted to storage molecules when abundant.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: Threats: insecticides, habitat loss, monoculture, pathogens and climate change. Conservation: flower strips, reduced pesticide use, habitat corridors, diverse planting and protected nesting sites. Link actions to food/resources and survival.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: Heritable variation exists; rare resistant insects survive treatment; susceptible insects die; survivors reproduce and pass resistance alleles; allele frequency rises over generations.

solution: Construction [1] Award for a coherent, logically ordered response using appropriate biological terminology.

stem: Water's molecular structure explains its roles in cells and plants.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Describe hydrogen bonding between water molecules.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Explain osmosis when an animal cell is placed in pure water.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Explain the cohesion-tension mechanism of transpiration.

questions.title: Water in living systems

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: Water is polar due to unequal electron sharing; oxygen is partially negative and hydrogen partially positive; attraction forms between H of one molecule and O of another; bonds are individually weak but numerous.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: Pure water is hypotonic/higher water potential; water crosses the selectively permeable membrane by osmosis; cell volume and pressure rise; without a wall the cell may lyse.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: Evaporation from mesophyll lowers water potential; water leaves through stomata; tension pulls xylem water upward; cohesion from hydrogen bonding maintains a continuous column; adhesion supports the column; roots replace lost water.
